target_customer: Young, app-first prepaid and postpaid mobile consumers in Brazil, initially university students, later also B2B clients
problem: Brazilians dislike traditional carriers that force unneeded data packages and make plan changes hard, with complaint rankings topped by telecom.
business_model: MVNO reselling Vivo network capacity via aggregator Telecall, sold digitally through an app with weekly or customizable plans

founders.name: Marcos Oliveira Jr
education: Engineering at USP (per Na Pratica article, March 2021)
founders.background_notes: Accepted into Programa Lideres Estudar in 2018 per napratica.org.br

founders.name: Vinicius Akio
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by napratica.org.br, not listed on the YC page

founders.name: Yuki Kuramoto
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by napratica.org.br, not listed on the YC page

investors: 603 retail investors via Kria equity crowdfunding

exit.reason: Aug 2022 report says Fluke cut over 80 percent of staff and agreed to a sale to an unnamed telecom company after a planned Series A fell through; completion not confirmed in sources found

competitors.name: Vivo and Claro app-managed plans
competitors.what: Large incumbent carriers offering plans contracted, controlled and supported through apps

competitors.name: Nomo
competitors.what: Another digital MVNO on the Telecall platform targeting consumers

technical_complexity.rationale: Built an app and billing layer on top of a rented Vivo network via Telecall, so no network engineering, but telecom integration and provisioning were required.

defensibility.rationale: The founder said wholesale network costs took about 93 percent of revenue in 2022 and the product sits on rented infrastructure, so incumbents and other MVNOs could copy the experience.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents already offered app-managed plans per Tecnoblog; Fluke ran out of runway in 2022 and agreed to a sale.

market_need_then: Telecom topped consumer complaint rankings in Brazil per Na Pratica (March 2021); Fluke had about one year of commercial operation in six states by March 2021.

branding.domain_note: Uses flu.ke, a domain hack, rather than an exact .com

identity.voice_and_tone: CEO frames the company as doing in telco what Nubank did in banking

brand_strength.rationale: Little press on the brand itself found; the name is shared with the unrelated test equipment maker Fluke Corporation, which dominates search results.

pivots.why: Startups.com.br headline says the company aims to double revenue in 2025 with a B2B focus

outcome_analysis: Fluke grew to about 100 staff and six states by 2021 and raised R$5 million by crowdfunding, but a planned Series A fell through in May 2022 and wholesale network costs of about 93 percent of revenue left no margin. It cut over 80 percent of staff in August 2022 and agreed to a sale to an unnamed telecom, then absorbed Nomo's consumer base in December 2023 and refocused on B2B.
notes: Company site returned HTTP 429. YC directory status Active, while the exit is recorded as unknown because the sale buyer and completion are unconfirmed. Crowdfunding investor count is 603 per dplnews and 621 per another outlet; a bridge and total near R$12 million are reported by one outlet only and left unrecorded as unverified. Databases list about 125K to 150K USD of early money from YC and angels, unverified. A private round target of about 1.34 million USD was reported by Yozzo and may not have closed. Founders named by Na Pratica beyond the YC page are included on that source. Competitors Vivo and Claro have no dated source. Nubank telecom was not a competitor as of 2021 per search results.
